claim: For N=3, B=Phi(|v-v_*|)b(cos(theta)), -3<gamma<=1, two-sided Phi(r)~r^gamma bounds, and two-sided angular bounds b(cos(theta))~theta^(-2-alpha) with 0<alpha<2, the linearized Boltzmann Dirichlet form around a fixed Maxwellian controls (i) the weighted L2 norm of h-P h from Theorem 1.1 and (ii) the local H^(alpha/2) norm of h-P h from Theorem 1.2. In particular b(theta)=a theta^(-2-2s), gamma=0, alpha=2s, 0<s<1 gives local H^s_v control for Maxwell molecules.
quantifiers_and_interface: For each admissible kernel B and every h in D(L_B), D_B(h)>=C_{gamma,alpha}||h-P h||^2_{H^(alpha/2)_loc(R^3)}. Precisely, for each fixed finite velocity ball B_R, this gives a positive c_R(B)>0 controlling the H^(alpha/2)(B_R) norm. P is the L2(M)-orthogonal projection onto span{1,v_1,v_2,v_3,|v|^2}. The theorem is velocity-only and has no spatial or time variable.
assumptions: -3<gamma<=1 and C_Phi r^gamma<=Phi(r)<=C'_Phi r^gamma for positive constants
fixed homogeneous Maxwellian; source convention F=M(1+h), L2(M dv)
h belongs to the domain of the linearized operator
proof_evidence: Primary source theorem read directly. Its proof restricts velocities to B_R, uses Carleman representation to lower-bound the positive jump term by the fractional difference integral with kernel |v-v'|^(-3-alpha), controls the cancellation remainder by a second-order Taylor expansion, and closes the L2 error with the Maxwell-molecule spectral gap. Near grazing angles the remainder is finite because integral_0^1 theta^(1-alpha)dtheta<infinity.

acquired: proof mechanism and equilibrium rescaling from the source paper

constant_dependence: The primary source states constructive dependence on gamma, alpha, radial and angular kernel comparison constants, and N. For the exact angular multiplier a, D_a=a D_1, hence the best local coercivity constant scales exactly linearly with a. For a lower angular multiplier a_- and radial lower bound C_Phi, positivity gives a valid lower coefficient at least C_Phi*a_- times the reference-kernel coefficient. The cancellation remainder in the source proof contains an angular integral O((1-s)^(-1)) when alpha=2s, so that proof does not furnish a uniform endpoint bound as s approaches 1. No optimal asymptotic in s was extracted.
costs: Infinite-dimensional functional input, no oracle or sample acquisition, and no finite bit or runtime cost. The constant is constructive at fixed parameters but no numerical lower bound was extracted here. The proof reports local ball constants with possible exponential growth in R.
strongest_comparator: Gressman-Strain 2011 Lemma 2.5 gives a stronger global anisotropic geometric fractional coercivity estimate in N^(s,gamma), under a closely matching non-cutoff kernel class.
falsifier: For one admissible fixed kernel and fixed finite R, construct h_j in D(L_B) with P h_j=0 and D_B(h_j)/||h_j||^2_{H^s(B_R)} tending to zero. Such a sequence would contradict the stated theorem.

claim: For a fixed homogeneous Maxwellian and x-independent collision kernel on T_L^3, local velocity coercivity lifts mode by mode: for every fixed R, L^-3 integral_T D(h(x,.))dx >= c_R(s,a) sum_{m in Z^3} ||(I-P)h_hat_m||^2_{H^s(B_R)}. The constant is independent of L and the spatial mode m.
quantifiers_and_interface: Fix 0<s<1, a>0, R<infinity, and L>0. Let h belong to L2(T_L^3;D(L_B)) and let h_hat_m be its normalized Fourier coefficients at k_m=2 pi m/L. Then the displayed inequality holds, initially for finite Fourier sums and by density for the stated domain. The spatial measure is normalized by L^-3; with unnormalized measure both sides acquire L^3.
assumptions: same kernel and Maxwellian as the primary local coercivity theorem
collision operator acts only in v and is independent of x
Fourier coefficients and D are in the domain needed for Parseval
proof: Since the collision form is local in x and quadratic, Parseval gives L^-3 integral D(h(x,.))dx=sum_m D(h_hat_m). Apply the primary source theorem to each coefficient; apply it separately to real and imaginary parts for complex modes. P acts only in v and is independent of m, so the sum of the mode inequalities is exactly the claim. No estimate of x derivatives is used.
constant_dependence: For B=a theta^(-2-2s) and gamma=0, c_R scales as a. Under Maxwellian M_{rho,u,T}, let lambda=sqrt(2T) and z=(v-u)/lambda. The source scaling is D_{rho,u,T}(h)=rho^2/pi^3 * lambda^gamma D_base(h(u+lambda z)); in z coordinates the coefficient for gamma=0 is rho^2/pi^3, independent of T and u. For physical v-patch norms, the L2 and homogeneous H^s pieces carry rho^2 lambda^(-3) and rho^2 lambda^(2s-3), respectively, on the patch B_{lambda R}(u). A positive lower density bound is necessary. The modewise c_R has no torus-length dependence.
costs: No new oracle, finite sample, or numerical computation. The derivation is one Parseval identity plus the source theorem; no arithmetic precision or conditioning cost is incurred. If the equilibrium parameters vary with x, Fourier modes couple and this corollary no longer follows as stated.
strongest_comparator: Gressman-Strain 2011 Lemma 2.5 controls a global anisotropic velocity norm and is stronger than the local isotropic H^s mode estimate. The current claim is useful only as an exact fixed-equilibrium Fourier lift.
falsifier: An admissible x-independent collision form for which Parseval fails to diagonalize the quadratic form, or a mode violating the source theorem, would refute the claim. For variable rho(x), u(x), or T(x), a counterexample to naive mode diagonalization is expected and that case is excluded.

claim: No positive lower bound ||(L_B+i v.k)q||_L2(M)>=c||q||_L2(M) can hold uniformly over all nonzero Fourier modes on tori of arbitrary side length L, even for the selected Maxwell-molecule non-cutoff kernel.
quantifiers_and_interface: For every L>0 choose k_L=(2 pi/L)e_1 and q(v)=1 in the relative-perturbation convention. With source Maxwellian M=e^(-|v|^2), ||(L_B+i v.k_L)q||/||q||=sqrt(2)pi/L, which tends to zero as L tends to infinity.
proof: The constant function q=1 is a collision invariant, so L_B q=0. Thus (L_B+i v.k_L)q=i(2 pi/L)v_1. The Gaussian M has variance 1/2 in v_1, so ||v_1||_L2(M)/||1||_L2(M)=1/sqrt(2). The ratio is sqrt(2)pi/L. Therefore any proposed L-independent positive coercivity constant is contradicted by this explicit sequence.
assumptions: same homogeneous Maxwellian and kernel as above
constant_dependence: The residual is exactly proportional to |k_L|=2 pi/L. The collision dissipation of the test vector is zero at every L. The inverse mean-zero torus Poincare scale is L^2/(4 pi^2).
costs: Closed-form calculation only; no numerical experiment, oracle, or approximation.
strongest_comparator: The modewise collision coercivity estimate controls only (I-P)q. Standard hypocoercivity estimates must add transport-macro coupling and retain the low-frequency torus scale; the local collision theorem contains no full-generator coercivity claim.
falsifier: A verified identity L_B 1 != 0 under the stated linearization, or a different norm in which the displayed Gaussian ratio stays bounded below as L grows, would invalidate this counterexample. Neither applies to the stated interface.
